response.rationale: Both answers are valid for the stated sense. Indonesian berantakan means disordered or untidy, while Malaysian Malay berselerak means scattered, untidily arranged, or not well organized. The different-common-word relation is appropriate. No false-friend contrast is present. Berselerak is not exclusive; bersepah is also a valid Malaysian alternative, but this is a preference/coverage issue rather than a learner-critical error.
